english.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a troubling feeling or the thing causing it.
Choose this when the unease is experienced as ongoing worry or personal troubles rather than mild disquiet.
Use this when stew means worry or a troubled state, rather than a food dish.
Use this for mental distress, worry, or a troubled state of mind rather than an external problem.

examples.english: Unemployment is my biggest worry lately.
examples.traditional: 失業係我最近最大嘅煩惱。
examples.jyutping: sat1 jip6 hai6 ngo5 zeoi3 gan6 zeoi3 daai6 ge3 faan4 nou5

examples.english: Money problems at home have caused me a lot of unease lately.
examples.traditional: 呢排屋企啲錢搞到我好多煩惱。
examples.jyutping: ni1 paai4 uk1 kei2 di1 cin4 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 hou2 do1 faan4 nou5

examples.english: It’s really not worth getting yourself in a stew over these little things.
examples.traditional: 為咗呢啲小事搞到自己咁煩惱，真係唔值得。
examples.jyutping: wai6 zo2 ni1 di1 siu2 si6 gaau2 dou3 zi6 gei2 gam3 faan4 nou5 zan1 hai6 m4 zik6 dak1

examples.english: Job hunting has been causing me a lot of trouble lately.
examples.traditional: 最近搵工搞到我好煩惱。
examples.jyutping: zeoi3 gan6 wan2 gung1 gaau2 dou2 ngo5 hou2 faan4 nou5
